title: SMF Capital
author: Adrian Lawrence
description: About SMF Unlocked SMF Unlocked is the podcast for anyone recruiting, holding, or thinking about taking on an FCA Senior Manager Function. Every episode unpacks a specific part of the Senior Managers and Certification Regime — what a designation like Chair, Chief Risk Officer, Compliance Oversight or MLRO actually requires, how the fit and proper test works in practice, and where boards and firms most often get SMF appointments wrong before it's too late to fix cheaply. This isn't a regulatory affairs show for compliance academics. It's a practical, direct look at SMF appointments from someone who runs these searches for a living — real patterns from real searches, the questions that actually separate a strong candidate from a risky one, and the mistakes that turn a straightforward appointment into a six-month Form A headache. About the host Adrian Lawrence FCA is a Fellow of the ICAEW and founder of SMF Capital, a UK recruitment practice specialising in FCA Senior Manager Function appointments — executive and non-executive. He founded FD Capital in 2018 and has since built out Exec Capital, NED Capital and Accountancy Capital alongside SMF Capital, working with boards, investors and regulated firms across the UK on senior and board-level appointments. He leads every SMF search personally, which is where most of what ends up in this podcast actually comes from. Who this is for Board members and non-executive directors navigating a Chair or committee chair appointment. Compliance and financial crime professionals building a case for their next SMF16 or SMF17 role. HR and governance teams trying to work out which designation actually applies to a role they're hiring for. And anyone who's been through an SMF appointment that went sideways and wants to understand why. New episodes regularly. Subscribe wherever you listen, and find detailed written guides to every SMF designation at smfcapital.co.uk.

title: Beyond the Injury: Understanding Serious
author: thomas edward
description:
Beyond the Birth is an informative and compassionate podcast dedicated to exploring birth-related injuries, medical negligence concerns and the challenges families may face when a baby experiences harm during pregnancy, labour, delivery or immediately after birth. The series aims to help parents understand complex medical and legal issues in accessible language while recognising the emotional impact that unexpected complications can have on an entire family.Each episode examines topics such as birth-related brain injuries, cerebral palsy, Erb’s palsy, shoulder dystocia, sub-galeal haemorrhage and trauma associated with instrumental delivery.

The discussions explore how medical records, labour monitoring, delivery decisions and independent medical opinions may help clarify what happened and whether the standard of care provided warrants further investigation.For parents seeking answers about a child's birth injury, birth trauma solicitors can provide information about the legal considerations involved, including how medical evidence is reviewed and how potential negligence claims are assessed.

The series highlights the importance of obtaining appropriate advice without assuming that every birth complication necessarily involves negligence.Beyond the legal questions, the podcast explores the realities of caring for a child with additional needs, accessing rehabilitation, planning for future care and navigating the emotional uncertainty that can follow a difficult birth. It also considers the importance of accountability, clear communication and ensuring that families have the information they need to make informed decisions.Through educational discussions, practical explanations and anonymised illustrative scenarios, Beyond the Birth seeks to empower families with knowledge, encourage thoughtful questions and explain the options that may be available when concerns arise. The series reflects the compassionate, evidence-focused approach associated with Cian O’Carroll Solicitors while making clear that each family's circumstances and legal options are unique.

Welcome to Four Questions, a podcast from Ayin Press about the power and art of questioning. 
At the heart of the Passover seder lie four questions: deceptively simple yet endlessly prismatic, they embody the ever-evolving Jewish tradition of inquiry. Four Questions draws on this sacred technology to stage a series of expansive and interdisciplinary conversations between artists, philosophers, activists, and teachers from distinct worlds. In each episode, two people meet through the vulnerable act of asking and answering four open-ended questions. Through a textured landscape of language, music, and silence, each question is revealed as a doorway, an invocation to the unknown. Rather than interviews, these conversations are intimate encounters whose themes reach across traditions and time spans—touching art, science, religion, theater, politics, and beyond. 
The show features guests such as multidisciplinary artist Cannupa Hanska Luger, Rabbi Jericho Vincent, philosopher Báyò Akómoláfé, Rabbi Nate DeGroot, writer adrienne maree brown, theater director Zhailon Levingston, and many more. 
At a time when so much media is transactional and reductive, Four Questions offers a glimpse of another kind of discourse. Grounded in Jewish wisdom, yet reaching far beyond it, Four Questions brings together diverse thinkers for wide-ranging conversations that explore the act of questioning as a spiritual, artistic, and universal practice.

title: Before & Beyond “ I Do” - Real talk about marriage at every stage
author: Susan Ortolano
description:
Before & Beyond “I Do” is the podcast for committed couples who want to create, or recreate a strong, deeply connected, conscious marriage designed to last.

Whether you’re engaged and already facing issues you don’t want to carry into your marriage, or you’re years beyond “I do” wondering, How the hell did we get here? this podcast offers real talk about what it actually takes to build, repair, and sustain a healthy partnership.

Intuitive Relationship & Marriage Coach Susan Ortolano goes beneath surface-level communication advice to explore the wounds, beliefs, protective patterns, and relationship dynamics quietly shaping how you show up with one another.

This is an inside-out exploration of marriage that goes deeper than the relationship advice you typically hear. You’ll gain insight into what is happening beneath your struggles, understand why your patterns persist, and learn practical ways to transform how you communicate, navigate conflict, rebuild trust, deepen intimacy, and consciously care for your partnership.

You’ll also come to understand Susan’s core, game-changing marriage philosophy: Marriage Success is an Inside Job™ and discover how changing the way you relate to yourself, your partner, and the challenges between you can transform your entire marriage.

Because strong marriages don’t magically happen. They are consciously created, or recreated by two people willing to take ownership, heal what needs to be healed, and grow individually and together.

And this is where the next chapter of your love story begins.

This week, we talk to Jeremy & Paul about the daily operation of running a small guitar shop and competing in the musical instrument marketplace in an era of big retail guitar chains, one click buying on music gear websites from your smartphone or laptop and the competition of marketplace scrollers.
So, is Logan Music, and independent guitar shops like them the 'Last of a Dying Breed?  Find out on this week's episode of The WNY Rocks! Podcast.

description: I started this wellness series after going through a complete rebirth of myself. My habits changed, my outlook on life changed, and I became a new person. title: Everybody Is Gonna Go Crazy
author: Jackson Scarlett
description:
Everybody Is Going To Go Crazy is a podcast-within-a-podcast about just how bad it can feel when everyone says you’re “crazy”—and just how good it can feel when you are. Using excerpts recorded during a 2021 medication-induced manic episode at the tail of the covid lockdowns, EGGC is a weekly vivisection of the things, people, and predicaments that are increasingly making everyone feel like they’re losing it.
EGGC is a podcast about psychiatry, religion, science, narcissism, covid politics… it’s a podcast about thinking. And thinking about thinking.
Join us weekly as we work through hours and hours of recordings made during my manic episode and try to figure out what the hell I was on about, and what it might mean for the rest of us as the world spirals out of control.

title: Local History Uncovering Forgotten
author: T JHEL
description:
Whispers from the Hollows: Forgotten Legends of Appalachia and the Pine Barrens
Short Description (for platform listings):
Three quiet legends that never made the history books — a road where cars roll uphill under the hands of Civil War ghosts, a demolished coal-camp house that once held a crying woman and a headless man, and the 300-year-old scream of the Jersey Devil.
Full Episode Description / Show Notes:
In a quiet stretch of road outside Burkittsville, Maryland, drivers still pull over at night, shift into neutral, and feel their cars begin to roll uphill. Locals say the ghosts of Confederate soldiers are still pushing.
In the New River Gorge of West Virginia, Company House Number 24 once stood in the vanished coal camp of Red Star. A family moved in during the 1930s and heard a woman crying, a baby wailing, and footsteps that belonged to a headless man. The company eventually tore the house down. The stories stayed.
And in the vast Pine Barrens of southern New Jersey, something with leathery wings and a horse-like head has been reported for nearly three centuries.
This episode of Local History travels the back roads of three places most people only pass through, uncovering the quieter legends that official history left behind.

Each episode addresses a relevant topic with an emphasis on reducing stigma, increasing awareness, and helping listeners recognize when emotional or behavioral difficulties may require professional attention. One key subject is dysregulation mood disorder, explored through an educational discussion of disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD), a condition associated with persistent irritability and frequent, intense temper outbursts in children and adolescents. The series helps listeners understand the difference between typical childhood frustration and ongoing difficulties that interfere with everyday life, relationships, and school experiences.

The podcast also discusses the importance of early assessment, supportive parenting approaches, therapeutic interventions, and individualized care. By presenting information in a respectful, nonjudgmental manner, Clearer Minds, Stronger Lives aims to help families feel better informed and more prepared to seek appropriate support from qualified healthcare professionals.

Through this intertextual approach, we uncover connections across Torah and Tanach, clarify difficult passages, compare and contrast seemingly different explanations, and address apparent contradictions within Rashi.

Rather than studying each Rashi in isolation, we seek to see the larger picture: how Rashi’s commentary in one place can unlock his meaning somewhere else.

Each weekly episode focuses on the Parsha and explores how Rashi’s own words throughout Tanach can deepen our understanding of his commentary on the Torah.

description:
Terence McKenna’s Blue Streak is an audio and video podcast about the life and work of Terence McKenna as seen through the Lux Natura Archive, produced in association with SpectreVision Radio.

Blue Streak offers a deep dive into the electric mind and mercurial voice of Terence McKenna — drawn from the vast range of audio recordings he generated in his lifetime, which are now in the Lux Natura Archive. Part excavation, celebration and time-travel, Blue Streak traces the arc of McKenna’s thought: from his iconic lectures on psychedelics, consciousness, creativity, language, and the living intelligence of nature — to raw, early rants crackling with intellectual audacity. Listeners will hear restored radio dialogues with late-night broadcasters, casual conversations recorded in the living room with fellow thinkers and friends, and field recordings captured in the Amazon during ethnobotanical adventures. The series also features dramatized readings from McKenna’s journals and letters, revealing a more vulnerable and personal current beneath his public persona. Blue Streak follows the streak itself — the rapid-fire, poetic, and mischievous verbosity that made McKenna a singular voice at the crossroads of psychedelics, philosophy, ecology, and the imagination. Hosted by his daughter, artist Klea McKenna, Blue Streak offers a living archive — a chance to receive a transmission from the edge.

title: Not Another Curbside: Training the Mind Behind the Medicine
author: MindShift MD | Chase Yonce, MD, Michele Demetriou, and Taylor Harris MD
description:
You know the curbside. You’re already behind, trying to get some lunch, and someone catches you in the hallway. Got a second?
Well, this is Not Another Curbside and it’s the conversation you’d actually choose to have. Two practicing physicians and a coach who works with professional athletes, CEOs, and high performers sit down each week with a quote or idea - from a legendary coach, an athlete, a thought leader, or occasionally Taylor’s grandfather - and break it down, test it against real life in medicine, and land on something you can use as a physician whenever you need it. Along the way, someone will probably invoke Michael Jordan, an epic movie, or the hip mobility of an NFL quarterback. It usually makes sense by the end.
This is for the doctor who doesn’t want more tips on managing burnout or another physician wellness module.
The premise is simple: the next level of physician performance is mental.
Medical training prepared you to diagnose, decide, and take care of everyone else. What it neglected to teach you is how to manage your own mind - when a case goes sideways, a patient is angry, the schedule implodes, or you’re home but your brain is still at work. That’s what Fierce Mind Management is: physician coaching meets mental performance training. Learning to respond instead of react. Pursuing excellence without demanding perfection. Treating a miss as information rather than a verdict. And managing your energy so the people at home get you, not what’s left of you.
Taylor (orthopedic surgery) and Chase (family medicine) are still in the trenches - still operating, still in clinic, and still making the most of every challenge. Michele has built a career coaching professional athletes, CEOs, and is bringing the same framework to medicine.
No doubt, medicine is a difficult field to succeed in. There will always be challenges, and a better mindset won’t cancel call. But how you meet pressure, recover from a miss, lead your team, and decide what an outcome means about you… that part can be trained and WILL make you a better physician.
No one gets great in isolation, even if medicine acts like you should. Come for the conversation. Stay for the brotherhood. Your lunch is already cold anyway.
Tune in if you’ve ever found yourself asking:
~ Why can’t I stop thinking about that case?
~ Why doesn’t time off fix physician burnout?
~ Is work-life balance actually possible for doctors?
~ How do I say no without feeling like I’m failing everyone?
~ Who am I when the white coat comes off?
~ How do I be present with my loved ones after a shift like that?
~ What do elite athletes and CEOs know that nobody teaches physicians?
~ Can physician coaching actually help me perform at work and be present at home?
Follow the podcast today and never miss an episode.

author: 𝐌𝐀𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐈̇𝐂𝐊® @trendexplorer
description:
Global Compass” is a podcast series dedicated to exploring the complex and ever-evolving tapestry of cultural, societal, and political dynamics shaping our world today. In a time where the world feels more interconnected yet increasingly divided, “Global Compass” serves as your guide through the intricacies of global affairs, offering insights and analyses that go beyond the headlines. Each episode is a deep dive into the stories, cultures, and events that shape our societies, revealing the underlying currents that influence how people live, think, and interact in different parts of the world.
At “Global Compass,” we believe that understanding the world requires a multifaceted approach—one that considers the historical, cultural, and social contexts that give rise to today’s pressing issues. Our episodes focus on the intersection of these forces, uncovering the narratives that shape nations, communities, and individuals. From exploring the cultural traditions that define a society’s identity to analyzing the global impacts of political decisions, we aim to provide a holistic view that connects the dots between seemingly unrelated events and trends.
In today’s fast-paced world, global issues often feel overwhelming, and understanding the ‘why’ behind them can be a daunting task. That’s where “Global Compass” steps in. We go beyond the surface to offer our listeners thoughtful and in-depth discussions, featuring expert interviews, firsthand accounts, and stories from people living through the events we cover. By listening to those directly impacted and incorporating expert analysis, we bridge the gap between local realities and global narratives, presenting a well-rounded perspective on critical issues.
The topics we cover span a broad range—from the politics that shape international relations to the social movements redefining community and identity. We dive into the cultural phenomena that bring people together and the divides that separate us. Whether it’s examining the economic policies of a powerful nation or understanding the impact of migration on local communities, “Global Compass” ensures each episode is both informative and thought-provoking, encouraging our audience to question, learn, and grow.
Each episode of “Global Compass” is meticulously crafted to engage, educate, and inspire. We use storytelling as a powerful tool to make complex subjects accessible and relatable. Our host guides listeners on a journey through history, geography, and culture, weaving narratives that reveal the interconnectedness of events and the ripple effects they have across borders. From the rise of new global powers to the impact of climate change on societies, we explore the challenges and opportunities that define the 21st century.
“Global Compass” also recognizes the importance of inclusivity and diversity in understanding the global landscape. Our episodes feature voices from a wide range of backgrounds, including journalists, historians, activists, and everyday people, to provide a comprehensive view of the issues at hand. By amplifying diverse perspectives, we aim to challenge preconceived notions and expand the conversation beyond conventional narratives.
Moreover, our show is not just about understanding the present; it’s about exploring the future. We look ahead to emerging trends and consider the potential paths societies may take. Whether discussing the future of technology and its impact on privacy, the role of youth movements in reshaping democracies, or the evolution of global economies, “Global Compass” offers insights that prepare listeners for the world to come.
